set.descent_text: The route finishes on the Alpine Garden, where a large boulder about thirty feet back makes a rope anchor. Walk toward the summit for a few hundred feet to meet the Alpine Garden Trail, then turn south toward Lion Head and drop down its trail to the Tuckerman Ravine Trail. Other ways off are the Escape Hatch on the left side of the ravine, or a line through the woods to the right that rejoins the approach trail but is less straightforward.
set.approach: From the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16, follow the Tuckerman Ravine Trail until the Huntington Ravine Fire Road branches right, then continue north past Harvard Cabin onto the open floor of the ravine. Damnation Gully is the longest gully and the second from the right end of the headwall; the buttress is the rock band immediately to its left. Climb the lower snow of the gully for several hundred feet until a dark, steep, prow-shaped wall appears at upper left. The technical climbing starts near there. The gullies sit below large snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast first.

review.notes: MP buttress page gives approach, finish on the Alpine Garden and three walk-offs; area page and newhampshireclimbing agree on the Tuckerman Ravine Trail and Fire Road toward Harvard Cabin. No distances given.

set.descent_text: The gully ends at the Alpine Garden. From there you can go back down the gully if you are comfortable on the steep snow, or head left along the Alpine Garden to the Escape Hatch, or follow the Lion Head Trail south along the Alpine Garden, which is the more scenic choice. Following the cairns instead leads to the summit and its trails or the auto road, but the road does not return you to Pinkham Notch and is only for emergencies.
set.approach: From the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16, follow the Tuckerman Ravine Trail until the Huntington Ravine Fire Road branches right, then continue north past Harvard Cabin onto the floor of the ravine. Central Gully is the low-angle gully just right of Pinnacle Gully and the Pinnacle Buttress, and it is one of the longest lines in the ravine. Slopes above it can slide, so check the avalanche forecast before you go.

review.notes: Descent from MP Central Gully location text; position from the Pinnacle Gully page; approach from area page and newhampshireclimbing.

set.descent_text: Rappel the route. It can be done in one or two stages, with a ledge partway up that serves as an intermediate station, and a slung block marks the top. Take enough rope that the long rappels reach, since a single short rope may not make the lower one.
set.approach: From the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16, follow the Tuckerman Ravine Trail until the Huntington Ravine Fire Road branches right, then continue north past Harvard Cabin onto the floor of the ravine. The climb is a dihedral with a right-facing corner, sitting low in Central Gully, not visible as you first arrive in the ravine until you have traversed out toward Damnation Buttress and Damnation Gully. Slopes above can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Rappel-the-route, ledge and rope note and the dihedral position from the MP Cloudwalker page.

set.descent_text: Near the top the gully forks, and bearing left through snow and frozen turf reaches the lip of the ravine, while a cornice can build on the direct line. From the lip, head south across the Alpine Garden toward Lion Head, or go east down the Escape Hatch. You can also follow the ravine rim west then south to above the top of the neighbouring gully and use its descent. Keep a compass handy if the weather turns.
set.approach: From the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16, follow the Tuckerman Ravine Trail until the Huntington Ravine Fire Road branches right, then continue north past Harvard Cabin onto the floor of the ravine. Damnation Gully is the second gully from the right end of the headwall and begins right beside the foot of North Gully. Crampon up the steepening snow into the deep, narrow gully; a short ice bulge comes after a few hundred feet. Check the avalanche forecast before you go.

review.notes: Gully top and cornice from the Damnation Gully page; walk-off options from the buttress and Odell's pages. Existing descent fact kept.

set.descent_text: This gully is as often used for descending as for climbing, and it is a quick way back to the ravine floor. From the top, find the big cairn where the Alpine Garden Trail meets the Huntington Ravine Trail, close to Central Gully's top-out, then walk down toward the ravine and diagonally left until the straight, narrow gully appears. The downclimbing is moderate, but a slip would carry you over the ice cliff at the bottom, so near it traverse to the left and downclimb or rappel as needed.
set.approach: From the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16, follow the Tuckerman Ravine Trail until the Huntington Ravine Fire Road branches right, then continue north past Harvard Cabin onto the floor of the ravine. The gully is largely hidden from the floor: work up toward the ice bulges, well to the right of Central Gully, until a narrow gully running diagonally upward comes into view. A steep ice cliff guards the entrance and can often be bypassed on the right. Check the avalanche forecast first.

review.notes: Everything on location, ice cliff and descent from the MP Diagonal Gully page.

set.approach: From the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16, follow the Tuckerman Ravine Trail until the Huntington Ravine Fire Road branches right, then continue north past Harvard Cabin onto the floor of the ravine. The line sits directly right of Cloudwalker, before Mechanic's Route, low on the headwall beside Central Gully. Slopes above can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Position relative to Cloudwalker and rappel descent from the MP Misty page; Cloudwalker page places that route low in Central Gully.

set.descent_text: Many parties rappel from fixed pins or rock horns a pitch or so up rather than continue. Going all the way to the crest is a long haul, farther than reaching the Alpine Garden via Damnation Gully, because the gully tops out near Nelson Crag.
set.approach: From the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16, follow the Tuckerman Ravine Trail until the Huntington Ravine Fire Road branches right, then continue north past Harvard Cabin onto the floor of the ravine. North Gully is the furthest-right gully of the ravine, next to Damnation Gully on its right. Move right across the fan until the ice bulge on the first pitch is easy to see. The slopes above are avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Location and descent from the MP North Gully page (single source for the rappel statement).

set.descent_text: Higher up, the gully eases onto far gentler ground just under the Alpine Garden. To descend, head south across the Alpine Garden toward Lion Head, or go more quickly east down the Escape Hatch. Carry a compass and know your bearing in case the weather worsens. The low-angle slope above this gully is prone to slides, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.approach: From the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16, follow the Tuckerman Ravine Trail until the Huntington Ravine Fire Road branches right, then continue north past Harvard Cabin onto the floor of the ravine. The gully is the wide open one immediately left of the Pinnacle Buttress. After an easy start, several moderate variations are available.

review.notes: Location and descent from MP Odell's page; approach from area page and newhampshireclimbing.

set.approach: From the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16, follow the Tuckerman Ravine Trail until the Huntington Ravine Fire Road branches right, then continue north past Harvard Cabin onto the floor of the ravine. The gully lies just right of the Pinnacle Buttress and left of the gentle Central Gully. Most trouble on this route comes from the snow above the ice, so check the avalanche forecast before you go.

review.notes: Position from MP and the ordering of gullies from Wikipedia. Descent left out: no read source says where the gully tops out.

set.descent_text: The usual way off is to walk down Central Gully. Take care, since slopes there can slide, and check the avalanche forecast.
set.approach: From the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16, follow the Tuckerman Ravine Trail until the Huntington Ravine Fire Road branches right, then continue north past Harvard Cabin onto the floor of the ravine. The climb is the pillar beside the start of Cloudwalker, low in Central Gully; it hangs over parties starting Cloudwalker.

review.notes: Single trip-style page; location and the Central Gully walk-off only. Page notes the line was previously unrecorded.

set.descent_text: The gully tops out on the Alpine Garden. From there walk south toward Lion Head, or use the Escape Hatch, the lowest-angle line, which lies just east of this gully. Both this gully and the Escape Hatch have a funnel-shaped top that can be a concern when avalanche danger is up, so check the forecast.
set.approach: From the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16, follow the Tuckerman Ravine Trail until the Huntington Ravine Fire Road branches right, then continue north past Harvard Cabin onto the floor of the ravine. South Gully is the furthest-left gully. Take the clear snow ramp along the far-left side of the fan below the headwall. Get local avalanche information before heading out.

review.notes: Top-out and location from MP South Gully; Escape Hatch position from its own page.

set.descent_text: The route ends on top of the Pinnacle Buttress. From the top, scramble up a loose talus slope to the flat Alpine Garden, rock-hopping to spare the fragile plants, and continue straight for several hundred yards to the well-cairned Alpine Garden Trail. Turn left on it, then take the Lion Head Trail down to rejoin the Tuckerman Ravine Trail for the walk out to Pinkham Notch.
set.approach: From the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16, follow the Tuckerman Ravine Trail until the Huntington Ravine Fire Road branches right, then continue north past Harvard Cabin onto the floor of the ravine. The climb begins on Pinnacle Gully's opening pitch, as far as the pin belay, then goes through the roofs on the north face of the Pinnacle Buttress. Check the avalanche forecast, and be mindful of parties on the gully below.

review.notes: Start and finish atop the Pinnacle from the Resistance page; Alpine Garden Trail to Lion Head descent from the Northeast Ridge page.

set.approach: From the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16, follow the Tuckerman Ravine Trail until the Huntington Ravine Fire Road branches right, then continue north past Harvard Cabin onto the floor of the ravine. The line begins at the foot of the ice bulge at the base of Central Gully. Slopes above can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Start and rappel descent from the MP Turf War page.

set.descent_text: The left fork of the gully leads to the top of the headwall. From there the usual ways down are across the Alpine Garden toward Lion Head, or the Escape Hatch. Use care at the lower end of the Escape Hatch, which comes out in the lower part of Yale Gully near an ice outcrop. Check the avalanche forecast before choosing a line.
set.approach: From the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16, follow the Tuckerman Ravine Trail until the Huntington Ravine Fire Road branches right, then continue north past Harvard Cabin onto the floor of the ravine. Yale Gully is the shallow gully next left of the easy-to-spot Damnation Gully, running to the lip of the ravine, with a small ice cliff a little left of its start. Begin up a long snow slope to a rope-length ice bulge.

review.notes: Gully layout from MP Yale page; Escape Hatch exit into lower Yale Gully from the AAC accident report. Walk-off options are inferred from neighbouring gullies since the Yale page does not describe the descent.
